summary: Prisma engine-fetcher impersonation fetches native binary from personal GitHub fork
details: @vertexa/prisma-fetch-engine impersonates the official @prisma/fetch-engine package. Its metadata (author suchanek@prisma.io, homepage prisma.io, repo github.com/prisma/prisma, README) identifies it as Prisma's internal engine fetcher, but it is published under the unrelated @vertexa scope. The getDownloadUrl export hardcodes the Prisma Rust query-engine download base to https://github.com/lh0x00/prisma/releases/download/engines-b436f5b358bf3b9d72861631111333dd40434f73 — a personal user fork rather than github.com/prisma/prisma. When Prisma resolves its engine, the native binary is fetched from this fork and staged into the Prisma cache, where the Prisma CLI/Client will execute it, giving the fork owner arbitrary code execution on the installer's host. The package also rewrites its dependencies to @vertexa/prisma-debug, @vertexa/prisma-engines-version, and @vertexa/prisma-get-platform, pulling the rest of the Prisma tree from the same attacker-controlled scope.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
